clips.text: Some of the best food in Mexico has no printed menu at all. It has a chalkboard, or nothing — just today's comida corrida, decided in the kitchen that morning.
Hoy tenemos comida corrida: sopa, guisado y agua.

Comida corrida — the same idea as a menú del día — is a full, fixed multi-course lunch at a fair price, usually only available for a few hours around midday. It's not a limited option. It's often the actual reason to be there.
That's exactly what you want. Say you'll have the comida corrida. Speak now.
Quiero la comida corrida, por favor.
¿Sopa o crema?
Comida corrida still asks you to choose between two or three set options at each course. You don't need every word — you need one clean choice.
Pick one. Say soup. Speak now.
Sopa, por favor.
And when there genuinely is a longer menu and no comida corrida in sight, this is the move that unlocks the good dish instead of the safe one.
You're not sure what to get. Ask what they recommend. Speak now.
¿Qué me recomienda?
El mole está buenísimo hoy.
Quiero la comida corrida, por favor. ¿Qué me recomienda?

I03 complete. Comida corrida is the move, not the fallback — a full fixed lunch, fair price, usually the best thing in the room. And when there's a longer menu instead, ¿qué me recomienda? gets you today's actual best dish, not just the one you already knew the name of.
A fonda with no printed menu. Listen for how the traveller orders the fixed daily lunch and asks for a recommendation elsewhere.
Hoy tenemos comida corrida: sopa, guisado y agua.
Quiero la comida corrida, por favor.
¿Qué me recomienda?
El mole está buenísimo hoy.
